metadata.explanation: Fischer esterification (or methylation, e.g., MeI/K2CO3) of the Boc-protected trans-4-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid gives the methyl ester precursor for subsequent reduction.

Reduction of the methyl ester to the primary alcohol (e.g., LiAlH4/THF or DIBAL-H) converts the Boc-protected amino ester into the Boc-protected amino alcohol. This ester-to-alcohol reduction is a dataset-matched analogous transformation.

N-Cbz protection of pyrrolidin-3-one via acylation of the secondary amine with benzyl chloroformate (Cbz-Cl). This mirrors the closely related, dataset-confirmed acylation of piperidin-4-one with Cbz-Cl (US05852040) to give the corresponding N-Cbz piperidinone; the analogous five-membered ring case follows the same well-established carbamate-forming chemistry (base-mediated Schotten-Baumann acylation).

N-Cbz protection of 3-hydroxypyrrolidine using benzyl chloroformate (Cbz-Cl), directly analogous to the dataset-confirmed reaction of 4-hydroxypiperidine with Cbz-Cl to give N-Cbz-4-hydroxypiperidine (US05932595).

Oxidation of N-Cbz-3-hydroxypyrrolidine to the corresponding ketone. This is directly analogous to the dataset-confirmed oxidation of N-Cbz-4-hydroxypiperidine to N-Cbz-4-piperidinone using pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC, generated in situ from CrO3/pyridine/HCl in isopropanol/DCM, US05932595); the same oxidation logic applies to the 3-hydroxy pyrrolidine analogue to deliver the 3-oxo pyrrolidine carbamate.

One-pot Strecker-type three-component reaction: N-benzyl-4-piperidone condenses with aniline to form an iminium/enamine, which is trapped by cyanide to give the alpha-aminonitrile; subsequent partial hydrolysis (nitrile -> primary amide) under acidic/basic aqueous conditions delivers the target alpha-anilino amide directly. This two-step sequence (condensation/cyanation then nitrile hydrolysis) is a classic route to 1-substituted-4-amino-4-carbamoyl piperidines used in fentanyl-analog chemistry.

metadata.explanation: Strecker-type three-component condensation of N-benzyl-4-piperidone, aniline, and potassium cyanide forms the alpha-aminonitrile via iminium formation followed by cyanide addition; standard conditions employ acid catalysis (e.g., AcOH/ZnCl2) or simple stirring in aqueous/alcoholic media at RT-reflux.

Two-step alternative: (1) Strecker-type reaction of N-benzyl-4-piperidone with aniline and cyanide (via the corresponding iminium ion) gives the alpha-aminonitrile intermediate 1-benzyl-4-(phenylamino)piperidine-4-carbonitrile; (2) controlled partial hydrolysis of the nitrile (e.g., H2O2/base or conc. H2SO4, short exposure) converts CN to the primary carboxamide without over-hydrolysis to the acid, furnishing the target amide. Splitting into isolable nitrile intermediate improves purification versus a fully one-pot process.
